title: Who left the study early?
hook: The lowest outcomes disappear from just one arm of an otherwise equal study.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: let sicker patients leave a study and watch a useless treatment look effective.

misconception: Treating who drops out? as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: let sicker patients leave a study and watch a useless treatment look effective.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Treatment and control both have outcomes 0,0,10,10. If only the treatment zeros drop out, what difference appears among completers?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-who-drops-out/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Treatment outcomes [0,0,10,10], control [0,0,10,10], bothmean5. Drop treatment zeros only: completer treatmentmean10 vs control5, apparent+5 from attrition.

claims.text: Selective dropout retains a completer difference of 5, while keeping every outcome retains 0. The low treatment outcomes disappeared; no outcome improved.

claims.text: Comparing completers can break the balance that assignment created. Whether missing outcomes can be recovered depends on the missingness assumptions and available follow-up information, not merely on having randomized the original invitation.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-who-drops-out/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Treatment outcomes [0,0,10,10], control [0,0,10,10], bothmean5. Drop treatment zeros only: completer treatmentmean10 vs control5, apparent+5 from attrition.

claims.text: Identical groups start with outcomes 2 and 8. Only the treated 2 disappears. What apparent mean difference remains? The treated completer mean is 8; the complete control mean is 5, so the difference is 3.
